dependencies.reason: Builds on OutputSchema on core.Tool to ensure wrapper tools and nested execution observe typed structured outputs.
Uses shell tool metadata definitions and guard.IsShellTool for transitive unguarded shell checks.

tasks.title: Add ReachableTools and Terminating fields to core.Tool and enforce cycle and terminating validation in agent constructors and registration
steps: In core/tool.go, add ReachableTools []Tool and Terminating bool to the core.Tool struct definition.
In core/tool.go, verify ToolWire and ToolWires functions project only Name, Description, InputSchema, and ConstrainedSampling, omitting ReachableTools and Terminating.
In agent.go, implement a depth-first traversal cycle detector for ReachableTools hierarchies.
In agent.go, update checkTool and checkCustomTools to validate reachable tool hierarchies: if a cycle is found, return an error matching 'agentkit: reachable tools cycle detected: <path>'.

In agent.go, update checkTool to verify that no wrapper tool declares a reachable tool with Terminating set to true, returning 'agentkit: terminating tool \"<terminating>\" cannot be reached through wrapper \"<wrapper>\"' if violated.
Ensure diamond dependencies without cycles are accepted without error during validation.

Write unit and property tests TS-07-1, TS-07-2, TS-07-3, TS-07-4, and TS-07-5 in core/tool_test.go and agent_test.go to verify declaration, wire projection, cycle rejection, terminating reachability restriction, and diamond dependency acceptance.

tasks.title: Implement transitive reachable tool queries, recursive policy resolution, and transitive unguarded shell tool checks
steps: In core/tool.go, implement core.ReachableTools(tools []Tool) []Tool computing the deduplicated transitive closure of all reachable tools, preserving the order of first appearance.
In agent.go, implement (*Agent).ReachableTools() []core.Tool by resolving the agent's ToolPolicy against registered tools and calling core.ReachableTools on the resolved set.
In core/toolpolicy.go, update ToolPolicy.Resolve to recursively filter ReachableTools of wrapper tools using NoTools, ToolNames, and ExcludeTools.
In core/toolpolicy.go, drop wrapper tools whose original ReachableTools was non-empty but is reduced to empty after filtering; retain leaf tools whose original ReachableTools was empty.
In execguard.go, update checkExecuteGuard to call core.ReachableTools on resolved tools when cfg.BeforeToolCall is nil.

In execguard.go, if an unguarded shell tool (guard.IsShellTool) is reachable through a wrapper, return an error wrapping core.ErrUnguardedExecute naming both the wrapper and the shell tool: 'agentkit: a shell tool is registered but AgentConfig.BeforeToolCall is nil; wrapper \"<wrapper>\" reached shell tool \"<shell>\"'.
Write unit tests TS-07-6, TS-07-7, TS-07-8, TS-07-9, TS-07-10, TS-07-11, TS-07-12, and TS-07-13 in core/toolpolicy_test.go and execguard_test.go.

tasks.title: Implement NestedCaller interface, context injection in executeBatch, and interceptor authorization and rewriting semantics
steps: In core/tool.go, define NestedCaller interface with Call(ctx context.Context, calls ...ToolUseBlock) ([]ToolResult, error), context key for NestedCaller, WithNestedCaller helper, and CallNested invocation helper.
In core/errors.go, define ErrNoNestedCaller, and ensure CallNested returns core.ErrNoNestedCaller when no NestedCaller is present in ctx.
In core/tool.go, add ParentToolUseID string and ParentToolName string to BeforeToolCallContext and AfterToolCallContext.
Create nested execution dispatcher in batch.go that binds parent tool-use ID, parent tool name, and resolved reachable tools.
In batch.go, when executeBatch prepares invocation for a tool with len(t.ReachableTools) > 0, inject the nested execution dispatcher into ctx via WithNestedCaller.

In the nested execution dispatcher, validate requested tool names against resolved reachable tools, returning ToolResult{OK: false, Error: 'unknown_tool', Detail: ...} and nil Go error for undeclared tools.

In the nested execution dispatcher, run BeforeToolCall with populated ParentToolUseID and ParentToolName: if Block=true and Terminate=false, return ToolResult{OK: false, Error: 'blocked_by_policy', Detail: reason} without aborting the wrapper or returning a Go error; if Block=true and Terminate=true, abort the wrapper and return core.ErrTerminated, propagating Terminate=true to the batch.
In the nested execution dispatcher, substitute non-nil Arguments from BeforeToolCallDecision before input validation and tool execution.

Write tests TS-07-14, TS-07-15, TS-07-16, TS-07-17, TS-07-18, TS-07-19, TS-07-20, and TS-07-21 verifying caller context, dispatcher injection, interceptor parent context, policy blocking, terminate propagation, and argument rewriting.

tasks.title: Implement terminating vote isolation, nested concurrency dispatch, execution modes, and cancellation handling
steps: In the nested execution dispatcher, implement terminating vote isolation: if an unmarked child tool handler returns ToolResult{Terminate: true}, override Terminate to false, set TerminateIgnored=true in the audit record, and annotate both the nested ToolResult Detail and wrapper ToolResult Detail that the terminate vote was ignored.

In the nested execution dispatcher, execute CallNested calls concurrently using goroutines joined by sync.WaitGroup when parallel tools is enabled and all invoked tools have ExecutionMode != core.Sequential.
In the nested execution dispatcher, execute CallNested calls sequentially in caller order when cfg.ParallelTools is false or any invoked tool has ExecutionMode == core.Sequential.
Ensure results in CallNested are collected and returned in the exact slice order corresponding to the input calls slice.
Isolate individual call failures (panics, handler errors, validation errors) so sibling nested calls in the same CallNested invocation complete unaffected.
Handle context cancellation in CallNested: abort in-flight nested tool calls and return ToolResult{OK: false, Error: 'aborted', Detail: 'Operation aborted'}.

Write tests TS-07-22, TS-07-23, TS-07-24, TS-07-25, TS-07-26, and TS-07-27 verifying terminating vote isolation, concurrent execution, sequential fallback, ordering preservation, sibling failure isolation, and context cancellation aborts.

tasks.title: Implement nested telemetry, events, audit records, subagent usage propagation, and transcript and stop policy isolation
steps: In core/event.go and core/eventjson.go, add ParentToolUseID string to ToolExecutionStartEvent, ToolExecutionUpdateEvent, and ToolExecutionEndEvent with omitempty JSON serialization.
In core/audit.go, add ParentToolUseID string and TerminateIgnored bool to AuditEvent.

In the nested execution dispatcher, generate a unique tool-use ID for each nested call and emit ToolExecutionStartEvent, ToolExecutionUpdateEvent, and ToolExecutionEndEvent with ParentToolUseID populated. Suppress ToolResultEvent emissions for nested calls.
In the nested execution dispatcher, emit an AuditEvent with Kind=AuditToolCall, ParentToolUseID, ArgumentsHash, error status, and elapsed duration upon completion.
In the nested execution dispatcher, wrap handler execution in a tracer span named 'agentkit.tool_call' recording tool_name, tool_use_id, parent_tool_use_id, and status attributes.
In the nested execution dispatcher, propagate core.WithUsageReporter on context to nested handlers so that subagent off-loop spend is credited to the agent immediately.
Ensure session recording (SessionStore) and conversation history (ConversationHistory) persist only the top-level wrapper tool call and result, omitting nested tool calls.
Ensure turn stop policies (including stop.WhenToolCalled) evaluate exclusively against top-level tool calls and results, ignoring nested tool calls.

Write tests TS-07-28, TS-07-29, TS-07-30, TS-07-31, TS-07-32, TS-07-33, and TS-07-34 verifying unique IDs, execution events, suppressed result events, audit logging, tracer spans, subagent spend reporting, history isolation, and stop policy scoping.
